norms.text: The first cup of the day's water is left at the hatching shed door.
Fish heads go to the clutch-keeper, never to the pot.
The roll is read on the barge, never in the camp.

taboos.text: Letting the hatching shed's fire go out.
Saying a hand's debt aloud in the camp.

values.text: A clutch kept warm until it hatches.
Every name on the roll known by the families.

contempts.text: Hands who leave the roll and leave their family to pay it.

place.text: A poor camp, kept clean, a short walk from the roll.

work.text: The gang dredges the port channel off the barge; the families keep the camp.

danger.text: Little hunts the slope; slugs and gar keep to the shallows.

rumour.text: Talk is of the clutch and of how long the debts will run.

directions.text: Ways are given from the shed: up to the Border road, down to the barge, out along the gang walk to the port.

addressTerms.text: Walker, to a stranger off the road; family names among themselves.

neverSaid.text: How much a named hand still owes.

grievances.text: The camp is a day from a Hist and has no claim on it.

rumours.text: More adults go downriver on the roll every year.

views.text: The house keeps the ledger and never comes to the camp itself.

dissent.text: She walks the doors for the house and believes the channel work ends each debt in time.
